assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reorganized international trade. It added within-industry reallocation and productivity-driven gains from trade to the earlier new trade theory. It also changed how trade is estimated with firm-level data and how trade policy is evaluated. The influence on empirical work, quantitative models and policy is very large.
assessment.attribution: The Melitz (2003) model is the clear core. Helpman's work on trade with differentiated products and on heterogeneous firms and FDI, with Melitz and Yeaple, gives a natural pairing. Redding is an important contributor with a quantitative and spatial extension, but his contribution is more recent and extends the core. Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are close contributors who are not on this ballot entry, so the credit boundary is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades have passed since the core result. Subsequent empirical and structural work has confirmed it extensively. The field has not been recognized since 2008, so timing is favourable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would treat Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as co-originators.
Helpman also appears in B001 on a different contribution, so the committee could prefer to combine or split his credit.
Some of the empirical gains-from-trade results depend on parametric assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks, with durable assets serving as both collateral and a factor of production. This is a foundational mechanism for credit cycles, now standard in macro-finance, in DSGE models with financial frictions and in policy analysis after the global financial crisis.
assessment.attribution: The credit-cycles paper and the related Kiyotaki–Moore work on liquidity and money are clearly attributable to the two. Bernanke and Gertler's financial accelerator is a closely related line. Bernanke has already been recognized, in 2022 with Diamond and Dybvig, and Gertler is credited elsewhere. A prize limited to Kiyotaki and Moore is therefore coherent.
assessment.maturity: The work is nearly three decades old, widely tested, and extended in both theory and quantitative models. Timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises could weigh against it.
Direct causal identification of the amplification mechanism is more indirect than in other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson, Tabellini and Besley built modern political economics. They made constitutions, electoral rules, accountability and state capacity objects of rigorous formal and empirical analysis, and connected political institutions to fiscal policy and development outcomes. The influence on later work is wide.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the most central, through their joint synthesis and empirical program on constitutions. Besley is central through work on accountability, state capacity and political agency. The three-name set is natural, but others such as Alesina, Acemoglu and Dixit also have strong claims in adjacent parts of the field.
assessment.maturity: The work has been developed over three decades and tested empirically. The 2024 prize on institutions shows the Committee's interest in the area, so the field is mature.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2024 institutions prize could be seen as redundant.
The credit boundary with Alesina (deceased), Acemoglu and Dixit is unclear.
Identification in cross-country constitutional comparisons is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the local labour market evidence on trade shocks changed how economists and policymakers think about automation, globalization, polarization and wage inequality. The influence on policy debate is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task and the China-shock literatures. Katz is central to the earlier skill-biased-change framework and to tasks. Hanson is central to the trade-shock evidence, with Dorn. Acemoglu and Restrepo have a related task-based theory and Acemoglu has already been honoured, so the grouping is a judgment about which contributions to credit. This choice is open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: The core work is 20 years old. The China-shock findings have been replicated and debated, and the task framework has been widely adopted. Recent debate about the size of effects does not weaken the central contribution.
uncertainties: Debate over magnitudes and external validity of the China-shock estimates.
Overlap with the Acemoglu–Restrepo task literature and with the 2024 prize.
Dorn could arguably replace Katz or Hanson.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models combine household heterogeneity, borrowing constraints and nominal rigidities, showing that the marginal propensity to consume and the distribution of wealth matter for how monetary and fiscal policy are transmitted. This restructured quantitative macroeconomics and central-bank modelling, and the continuous-time methods spread widely.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante (2018) are clearly the core. Auclert, Bilbiie, Werning, Krusell, Smith and others are closely related. Because Krusell is the secretary of the committee, the committee should note the broader lineage of the heterogeneous-agent literature when deciding credit.
assessment.maturity: The framework is under ten years old, and long-run empirical confirmation of its policy implications is still limited. The underlying ideas have deeper roots in the Aiyagari–Bewley–Huggett tradition. It is likely too early.
uncertainties: Early for a prize, and the quantitative literature is still developing.
Attribution relative to the Aiyagari/Bewley/Huggett lineage and to Auclert, Werning and others.
Disclosure: this is close to my own research area and I have collaborated with committee colleagues in related heterogeneous-agent work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) showed how resource misallocation across firms can account for much of the cross-country difference in TFP, giving a measurement framework that spread across growth and development economics. The impact on how economists link micro-level distortions to aggregate income is large.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow carry the most prominent contribution. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) developed the misallocation idea simultaneously and independently, and Rogerson is not on the ballot entry, so the credit boundary is a real concern. Restuccia could be added in place of or in addition to Klenow.
assessment.maturity: The main contributions are about 17 years old and have been much extended, including with careful microdata. Debate about measurement error in the wedges remains.
uncertainties: Disclosure: Klenow is a long-running co-author of mine, which could affect how my ranking is read.
Whether the wedge-based measurement is robust to measurement error and to adjustment costs.
Credit shared with Restuccia and Rogerson, and with Banerjee and Duflo on misallocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's alternating-offers model gave the standard strategic foundation for bargaining and linked it to the Nash solution. The Rubinstein–Wolinsky market bargaining work introduced decentralized trade with search. The ideas are used throughout theory, labour, macro and industrial organization.
assessment.attribution: The 1982 alternating-offers result is Rubinstein's. Wolinsky's contribution lies in markets with bargaining and search. Binmore's connection to the Nash program and the outside-option interpretation is real but more derivative. Stahl's earlier related finite-horizon work is a further attribution issue.
assessment.maturity: The work is more than four decades old and canonical. Game theory has been honoured several times, so the main consideration is whether the committee wants another theory prize.
uncertainties: Recent game-theory prizes (2020 auctions, 2007 mechanism design) may crowd out another theory award.
Whether Rubinstein alone should be honoured, given that the Wolinsky contribution is more specialized.
Relative claims of Binmore and Stahl.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large administrative datasets were used to measure intergenerational mobility, to map it across places, and to estimate neighbourhood effects. This changed empirical public and labour economics and opened data-based policy design. The scale and policy influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the central figure. Hendren is central to the causal place-effects and neighbourhood work. Friedman and Katz are important co-authors, with Katz also credited on the Moving to Opportunity evidence. Credit is spread across a large team, which makes a three-person limit hard.
assessment.maturity: The core mobility results date from about 2014 onward and the place-effects work from 2018. This is relatively recent for a prize, though replication of the descriptive facts is good. Long-run validation of policy implications is still open.
uncertainties: Early relative to the other candidates, and the policy implications are still being tested.
Team-based attribution among Chetty, Hendren, Friedman, Katz and others.
Methodological debate about the identification of place effects and the measurement of mobility.
